newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN WINS FOR WILLIAMS IN SAN MARINO.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN WINS FOR WILLIAMS IN SAN MARINO.

text.p: German Heinz-Harald Frentzen opened up the battle for the world drivers' championship on Sunday when he claimed his first formula one victory by winning the San Marino Grand Prix.

Frentzen, 29, driving a Williams, capitalised on the retirement of team mate and world championship leader Jacques Villeneuve of Canada by dominating the second half of an eventful race and finishing 1.2 seconds ahead of compatriot Michael Schumacher.

Double world champion Schumacher, in a Ferrari, did his best to deliver victory for fans on the team's home circuit but was ultimately frustrated by the Williams superiority. Ferrari team mate Briton Eddie Irvine finished third.
Italian Giancarlo Fisichella was fourth for Jordan, scoring his first world chmapionship points, ahead of Frenchman Jean Alesi in a Benetton and Mika Hakkinen of Finland in a McLaren.
The result hoisted Frentzen into equal third place in the title race behind Villeneuve who leads with 20 points from Schumacher on 14.
Villeneuve, starting from his fourth successive pole position, led for the opening 26 laps before pitting for the first time. He was third from there until lap 41 when he retired.

Defending world champion Damon Hill of Britain started from the pit lane in his Arrows and crashed out after only 12 laps in a collision which also removed Japan's Shinji Nakano, in a Prost, from the race.
